subject: Quantimed: data residency & isolated hosting follow-up
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.h@quantimed.com>, Mark Zhou <mark.z@quantimed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Quantimed: data residency & isolated hosting follow-up

Hi Lisa / Mark — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Top-level goals you shared:
- Keep PHI and derived models inside Quantimed-owned network for residency and auditability.
- Avoid any outbound traffic from compute that would land in public multi-tenant clouds.
- Meet your auditors' requirements for key management and retention (you mentioned HSM / FIPS requirement).

Primary pain points:
- No public IPs on inference hosts and strict egress policies — currently all outbound must go via the corporate proxy with allowlist.
- Procurement timeline: need a cost estimate and SOW to start budget approvals; target pilot in Q1 2027.
- Ops: limited room for frequent model updates due to change-control (air-gapped update path preferred).

Assumptions we made during the call (please correct if wrong):
1) You can provision a dedicated VLAN and route to an on-prem appliance or Direct Connect partner for outbound telemetry (no direct public egress).
2) Audit logs and request traces can be delivered to your SIEM via a push to an internal collector (we will not send logs to Redwood hosted account unless you opt in).
3) Initial pilot is 3 machines (N+1) for inference with 30k requests/day, then scale-by-commit if pilot succeeds.

Open technical questions (need answers before we size SOW):
- Is a hardware HSM required for encryption keys at rest, or will a KMS inside your VPC suffice?
- Which outbound ports/proxies are allowed to contact vendor endpoints (if any)? Do you allow TLS egress to specific hostnames?
- Maximum acceptable RTO/RPO for model updates and whether offline (sneakernet) delivery is required.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
- Rafael: provide a hosting options matrix (redwood private on-prem appliance vs. virtual private deployment) + cost ranges — by 2026-11-30. (Attachment: redwood-hosting-options-matrix.xlsx)
- Marissa: schedule a technical discovery (VPN/Direct Connect, allowed ports, HSM details) — propose 2026-12-02 or 2026-12-03.
- Quantimed (Lisa/Mark): confirm whether HSM is mandatory and share procurement contact for an initial budget ask.

Attachments: architecture sketch (high-level), hosting matrix, and a draft SOW skeleton.

If the summary looks correct, reply-all with any corrections and which day/time works for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Hammond <lisa.h@quantimed.com>

Date: 2026-11-27T18:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quantimed: data residency & isolated hosting follow-up

Thanks Rafael — this is a good summary. A few clarifications from our side: we do require FIPS 140-2 validated HSM or HSM-backed keys for any envelope encryption of PHI at rest. A cloud KMS inside our VPC is acceptable only if it is backed by an HSM that meets that standard.

On egress: our policy today disallows any outbound connections from compute nodes unless routed through the corporate proxy (they perform TLS inspection). We will not allow connect-to-service patterns that rely on public IPs from inference hosts. If Redwood needs to reach out to the control plane during inference, that traffic must terminate on endpoints we explicitly approve and through our proxy.

Model updates: for the pilot we prefer an air-gapped update approach — deliver artifacts to a secure staging host inside our network and we will run controlled deploys. Frequent remote model pulls are not permitted without a formal change-control exception.

Procurement: procurement@quantimed.com (cc'd) will need an order-of-magnitude monthly cost + a short SOW to start internal approvals. Please include a line for one-time on-prem appliance setup and a separate recurring license/maintenance item.

We can do the technical deep-dive on 2026-12-02 at 11:00 PT. Mark will join for the network portion.

— Lisa Hammond
Director of Product Security, Quantimed Health

Thanks — copying in a few technical clarifications from infra so the deep-dive is focused:

1) Connectivity model options we should be prepared to discuss:
   - Private appliance (customer-owned hardware in their DC) with LAN access to inference hosts and a one-way outbound channel to Redwood for telemetry (if allowed).
   - Redwood Private deployed inside Quantimed VPC / project with no public endpoints; control plane connectivity via approved proxy endpoints.
   - Fully air-gapped: S3-like artifact handoff + on-prem installer and no outbound connectivity.

2) Questions for Quantimed to confirm during the deep-dive:
   - Do you have an existing Direct Connect / ExpressRoute circuit we can leverage, or should we plan for a VPN termination?
   - Which proxy certificates / hostnames can we include in our allowlist for optional outbound telemetry? Please provide a sample allowlist if available.
   - Can your security team sign off on a signed SSH key rotation process for the appliance (we recommend short-lived keys for ops access)?

3) For the SOW we will break costs into: appliance one-time install, secure-MTU network engineering time, and recurring license + remote support retainer.

Rafael — I will take the network/ops portion of the discovery. 2026-12-02 11:00 PT works for me. I’ll send a calendar invite and draft an internal checklist for the call.

— Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
